prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (ideology and names omitted)

- Family, tax and work
  - Targeted tax cuts: higher Children’s Tax Credit for under‑5s; a new allowance for couples with young children or caring responsibilities; higher age‑related personal allowance removing around one million pensioners from income tax; abolish most taxes on savings/dividends; cut fuel duty by at least 6p/litre; selected business tax reductions; repeal IR35.
  - Reform Working Families Tax Credit to be paid direct to the caring parent; scholarships to help parents re‑enter the workforce; remove tax on Widowed Parent benefits.

- Schools and universities
  - Autonomy for all schools (“Free Schools”): heads/governors control budgets, staffing and admissions via home‑school agreements; easier exclusion of disruptive pupils; creation of Progress Centres; allow successful schools to expand and new schools (including faith/parent‑led) to open; parents can trigger inspections leading to management change.
  - Students repay loans only above £20,000 income; no top‑up fees; create permanent endowments to increase university independence.

- Policing, crime and justice
  - Increase police numbers; cut bureaucracy; visible policing (“cops in shops”); parish constables.
  - Tenfold increase in places for persistent young offenders; tougher action on drug dealers (mandatory jail for sales to under‑16s; aggravated sentences near schools).
  - “Honesty in sentencing” (end automatic early release); require prisoners to work with proceeds to victims/families; lifetime supervision available for sex offenders; protect children online.
  - Stronger victim rights, including named contacts and reasons for charge changes; review self‑defence and double jeopardy laws.

- Economy, spending and regulation
  - Return £8bn annually in targeted tax cuts funded by savings not affecting schools, the NHS, police or defence.
  - Transparency measures: clear taxpayer statements; National Accounts Commission; simpler capital gains tax.
  - Deregulation: a powerful Deregulation Commission, regulatory budgets reduced yearly; exemptions for small firms.

- Health
  - Match planned NHS funding but end political micromanagement; Patient’s Guarantee of maximum waits by clinical need (starting with cancer/cardiac), with treatment elsewhere (including private) if breached.
  - Restore ward‑level authority (ward sisters/matrons); patient/GP choice of hospital with performance data; expand practice nurse roles; NHS‑funded specialist surgical centres; Exceptional Medicines Fund; increase state hospice funding to 40%.

- Pensions and care
  - Increase basic state pension (larger rises for over‑75s); option to consolidate certain payments into a higher tax‑free pension; end compulsory annuitisation at 75; consult on funded alternatives for younger workers; protect pre‑funders of long‑term care.

- Europe, defence, foreign affairs
  - “In Europe, not run by Europe”: keep the pound and national veto; seek treaty flexibility and domestic “reserved powers”; strengthen the single market and EU anti‑fraud controls.
  - Prioritise NATO; oppose EU military structures outside NATO; support ballistic missile defence; maintain independent nuclear deterrent.
  - Aim for 0.7% GNP in aid, double the share via charities; create “Aid Direct”; pursue a trans‑Atlantic free trade area and global free trade by 2020.

- Asylum
  - House new applicants in secure reception centres until decisions; presume refusal from safe countries; create a Removals Agency for rapid deportation of rejected cases.

- Welfare and civil society
  - Office of Civil Society; remove charities’ irrecoverable VAT (funded by scrapping euro‑prep budgets); replace New Deal with payment‑by‑results “Britain Works” focused on sustained jobs; “Can Work, Must Work”; lone parents with children over 11 to seek suitable work; improve disabled savings rules; new incapacity agency with rehabilitation funding; national anti‑fraud taskforce and NI number cleanup.

- Town, country, transport, environment
  - Foot‑and‑mouth recovery plan; seek national control within CAP/CFP; clear origin/method food labelling; strengthen animal welfare.
  - Support rural services (rate cuts, fuel rebates for community transport, benefit card to sustain post offices); scrap central housebuilding targets; protect “Blue Belts”; rural select committee.
  - Urban regeneration companies with powers; tougher action on nuisance tenants; prioritise brownfield; expand right‑to‑buy/rent‑to‑mortgage; homesteading grants.
  - Long‑term transport plans; Roads Standards Unit; consider 80mph where safe; charge foreign lorries; rail safety upgrades.
  - Meet climate goals via emissions trading, conservation, incentives, renewables and cleaner generation; review nuclear; replace the Climate Change Levy package.

- Culture, media and sport
  - Endow arts/cultural bodies via Channel 4 sale and Lottery surpluses; simplify Lottery access; tourism promotion; protect school sport time/playing fields; charitable status for local sports clubs.
  - Single media/communications regulator; privatise Channel 4 (retain public service remit); modernise ownership rules; independent BBC regulation; fair access for religious broadcasters.

- Democratic reform
  - Devolve powers to high‑performing “free councils”; local referendums for large council tax rises; abolish regional agencies/assemblies; restrict voting on England/Wales‑only laws to relevant MPs; reform Lords via independent appointments and a substantial elected element; strengthen parliamentary scrutiny; retain current general election voting system; reduce numbers of ministers, MPs (after reforms) and special advisers; uphold consent‑based settlement in Northern Ireland.
